title: Graham's Law of Diffusion/Effusion

references.label: NCERT Chemistry Part I, Class 11 — States of Matter

expression: r1/r2 = √(M2/M1)  (at the same temperature and pressure)
explanation: Graham's law states that the rate of diffusion (or effusion) of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass, at constant temperature and pressure — lighter gases diffuse/effuse faster than heavier gases. This follows directly from kinetic theory, since lighter molecules have a higher RMS speed at the same temperature (average kinetic energy is the same for all gases at a given T, so lower mass means higher speed).

variables.meaning: Rate of diffusion/effusion of gas 1 and gas 2
Molar mass of gas 1 and gas 2

workedExample.scenario: Compare the diffusion rates of H₂ (M=2) and O₂ (M=32) at the same conditions.
workedExample.result: H₂ diffuses 4 times faster than O₂

commonMistakes: Forgetting the relationship is inverse and involves a SQUARE ROOT, not a direct or simple inverse ratio of molar masses — a very common calculation slip.
Applying Graham's law to compare gases at DIFFERENT temperatures or pressures — the law strictly assumes both gases are compared under the SAME temperature and pressure conditions.
genZNote: Graham's law: lighter gas, faster escape — mass and speed are in an inverse square-root relationship.
